title: clagentic: loadout common schema fragments
description:
Shared fragments referenced by the dispatch envelope schemas (envelope-in.json, envelope-out.json). Field definitions here are authoritative for the published loadout contract set.

contract_revision common@2: added the `followup` fragment (a generic, minimal work-item descriptor used by envelope-out.json's `followups[]`). All prior fragments are unchanged -- this is an additive migration. NOTE: the $id path segment stays `v1` because sibling schemas in this directory resolve `$ref: "common.json#/..."` relative to their own base URI (same directory) -- bumping this file's $id alone breaks that relative resolution for every other schema here. A package-wide $id version bump is a separate, coordinated release decision, not a per-file one; see docs/integration.md's "Envelope contract versions" section for the tracked contract_revision numbers.

task_id.description: Opaque work-item identifier scoping this invocation. Shape is deployment-defined (a task tracker key, ticket ID, or any stable string); loadout does not assume a specific tracker or ID pattern.

commit_sha.description: Full (non-abbreviated) git commit SHA, lowercase hex, exactly 40 characters. Every SHA field in an envelope is a typed value validated at compose time, not a hand-carried string compared downstream. A shorter abbreviated form must be resolved to the full 40-character value (e.g. via `git rev-parse`) before it is placed in a field that uses this fragment; consumers normalize surrounding whitespace before validating but do not relax the 40-character requirement.

project.description: Target project name. Resolves against the deployment's own project registry; loadout treats this as an opaque identifier.

agent_name.description: Normalized lowercase role/agent identifier (e.g. 'builder', 'reviewer', 'merger'). The published contract declares the SHAPE only — which concrete names or roles are valid for a given deployment is supplied by that deployment's own cast/roster configuration, never by this schema.

name.description: Resolved human identity. Canonical form only — no aliases; canonicalization is a deployment concern.

actor.description: A structured human or agent identity ({kind, name}). Used in invoker and participants[], and is one accepted shape for authorized_by. See #/$defs/authorized_by for the field that also accepts a plain-string provenance form.

oneOf.description: Provenance string form. Any non-empty provenance string is accepted at the shape level — this is not an enum of literal names; freeform provenance parentheticals (e.g. an approving identity plus context) are legitimate. The load-bearing SEMANTIC constraint (an autonomous agent must never self-authorize a release-gated action) is enforced by the deployment's merge-gate logic, not by this schema.

authorized_by.description: Who approved this work. Accepts either the structured actor object ({kind, name}) or a plain provenance string. For release-gated actions the approving identity must resolve to a human or an authorized project role — never an agent authorizing itself; that check happens at the deployment's merge gate, not here.

invoked_by.description: Who dispatched this specific invocation. May equal authorized_by or may be an intermediate orchestrator.

name.description: Canonical human identity. No aliases; canonicalization is a deployment concern.
Agent/role name. Validated against the shape only — mapping a name to a concrete cast entry is a deployment concern, not this schema's.

participant.description: A single participant in a conversation. Shape mirrors actor: oneOf{human, agent} so that name shape is mechanically enforced for agents.

participant_role.description: Enumerated participant role. No freeform values.

participant_position.description: Ordering within the participants array. Stable across retries of the same invocation.

conversation_id.description: UUIDv7, issued exactly once per top-level dispatch. Inherited by every child, sibling, and retry invocation in the tree. Retries do NOT mint a new conversation_id — they increment attempt. Globally unique across a deployment.

invocation_id.description: UUIDv7 for a single agent invocation. Distinct from conversation_id: a conversation may contain many invocations.

attempt.description: Retry counter for this invocation_id. First attempt = 1. The dispatching layer increments on retry; agents never touch this.

invocation_ts.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the dispatching layer constructed the envelope.

status.description: ok: work completed as contracted. failed: agent tried and could not complete (bug, infra, transient). blocked: agent refused because preconditions were not met (gating criteria failed, inputs invalid). blocked is not an error — it is a valid outcome for a gate-role agent.

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. No free-form error strings in envelopes — prose goes in the linked result artifact, not the trace.

agent_result_path.description: Reference to the agent's full result artifact (a path, URI, or deployment-defined locator). The concrete storage convention — where results live and how they are addressed — is deployment configuration, not part of this published contract. The artifact may contain prose, diffs, and tool output that are explicitly forbidden from the envelope itself.

summary.description: Short, non-prose description of the follow-up work item. Detailed context belongs in the result artifact (agent_result_path), not here.

kind.description: Deployment-defined categorization (e.g. 'refactor', 'security', 'docs'). Open string, shape-only -- loadout does not enumerate valid kinds.

related_path.description: Optional file or resource path the follow-up concerns. Opaque to loadout.

priority.description: Optional coarse priority hint. A deployment's own consumer decides what to do with it; loadout assigns no other meaning.

followup.description: A generic, minimal work-item descriptor. This is NOT a task-tracker record -- it carries no tracker ID, no assignee, no status. loadout defines only the SHAPE; whether and how a deployment turns this into a tracked task (or does nothing with it) is entirely that deployment's concern (CLAUDE.md hard rule 6a).
